changes.why: CHK-006 updated shadow_en only at the D handshake and checked every bit with shadow_en=0 between the A handshake and the D handshake. During that window, under D-channel back-pressure, the design may already apply the write. No document says whether a write takes effect at A or at D, and D-018 only binds o_intr_gpio outside the 2 cycles after INTR_ENABLE changes. The fix masks only the bits that an outstanding INTR_ENABLE write sets from 0 to 1, from its A handshake until Ed; the existing masks at Ed and Ed+1 are kept. Bits that are 0 in both the old and the new value are still checked on every edge, and so are the bits a write clears (1 to 0) from Ed+2.

CHK-008 fired at the t=0 clock edge. At that point rst_ni has never been asserted: there was no falling edge and no clock edge processed with rst_ni=0, and no document defines a power-on state. The check now starts at the first reset assertion, which is the first falling edge of rst_ni or the first rising clock edge processed with rst_ni=0. The flag is never cleared, so every later edge with rst_ni=0 is checked, including the first clock edge after rst_ni falls asynchronously (contract CHK-008). The hit counter used the condition `!(!rst_ni) && (!rst_ni)`, which is never true. It now counts the edges where the check is active. The fail message now prints the six output values to show the root cause.
changes.content:
module nnc_chk_reset #(
  parameter int GpioAsyncOn = 1,
  parameter int GpioAsHwStrapsEn = 1
) (
  input  logic                        clk_i,
  input  logic                        rst_ni,
  input  logic                        i_a_valid,
  input  logic                        o_a_ready,
  input  logic [2:0]                  i_a_opcode,
  input  logic [2:0]                  i_a_param,
  input  logic [1:0]                  i_a_size,
  input  logic [7:0]                  i_a_source,
  input  logic [31:0]                 i_a_address,
  input  logic [3:0]                  i_a_mask,
  input  logic [31:0]                 i_a_data,
  input  logic                        i_a_instr,
  input  logic                        i_a_intg_flip,
  input  logic                        o_d_valid,
  input  logic                        i_d_ready,
  input  logic [2:0]                  o_d_opcode,
  input  logic [2:0]                  o_d_param,
  input  logic [1:0]                  o_d_size,
  input  logic [7:0]                  o_d_source,
  input  logic                        o_d_sink,
  input  logic [31:0]                 o_d_data,
  input  logic                        o_d_error,
  input  logic                        o_d_intg_err,
  input  logic                        o_alert,
  input  logic                        o_alert_integ_fail,
  input  logic [31:0]                 i_gpio,
  input  logic [31:0]                 o_gpio,
  input  logic [31:0]                 o_gpio_en,
  input  logic [31:0]                 o_intr_gpio,
  input  logic                        i_strap_en,
  input  logic                        o_straps_valid,
  input  logic [31:0]                 o_straps_data
);

  int unsigned fails_CHK_008 = 0;
  int unsigned hits_CHK_008 = 0;

  // NNC verification fix (fix-verif, triage B): D-016 binds the outputs 'while rst_ni = 0', i.e. once reset has been
  // asserted; no document defines a power-on state before the first assertion (time 0). rst_seen_q is set at the
  // first falling edge of rst_ni or at the first rising clock edge processed with rst_ni=0 and is never cleared, so
  // every later edge with rst_ni=0 is checked, including the first clock edge after an asynchronous assertion.
  logic rst_seen_q = 1'b0;
  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) if (!rst_ni) rst_seen_q <= 1'b1;
  wire chk008_ante = rst_seen_q && !rst_ni;

  // CHK-008: Outputs held at zero during reset (GP-10-31, GP-10-03, GP-2-06)
  a_CHK_008: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) chk008_ante |-> (o_d_valid == 1'b0 && o_alert == 1'b0 && o_alert_integ_fail == 1'b0 && o_intr_gpio == 32'h0 && o_gpio == 32'h0 && o_gpio_en == 32'h0))
    else begin fails_CHK_008++; $display("NNC_FAIL CHK-008 @%0t o_d_valid=%0b o_alert=%0b o_alert_integ_fail=%0b o_intr_gpio=%h o_gpio=%h o_gpio_en=%h", $time, o_d_valid, o_alert, o_alert_integ_fail, o_intr_gpio, o_gpio, o_gpio_en); end
  // NNC verification fix (fix-verif, triage B): the hit condition was '!(!rst_ni) && (!rst_ni)' (never true); count the edges where the check is active.
  always_ff @(posedge clk_i) if (chk008_ante) hits_CHK_008 <= hits_CHK_008 + 1;

  // CHK-008: same check on the falling clock edge (GP-10-31, GP-10-03, GP-2-06)
  a_CHK_008_neg: assert property (@(negedge clk_i) chk008_ante |-> (o_d_valid == 1'b0 && o_alert == 1'b0 && o_alert_integ_fail == 1'b0 && o_intr_gpio == 32'h0 && o_gpio == 32'h0 && o_gpio_en == 32'h0))
    else begin fails_CHK_008++; $display("NNC_FAIL CHK-008 @%0t o_d_valid=%0b o_alert=%0b o_alert_integ_fail=%0b o_intr_gpio=%h o_gpio=%h o_gpio_en=%h", $time, o_d_valid, o_alert, o_alert_integ_fail, o_intr_gpio, o_gpio, o_gpio_en); end

  final begin
    $display("NNC_CHECK CHK-008 hits=%0d fails=%0d", hits_CHK_008, fails_CHK_008);
  end
endmodule

changes.why: Rule (f) compared a 49-bit truncation of a 122-bit concatenation. It covered only i_strap_en, i_gpio, i_d_ready, i_a_intg_flip, i_a_instr and i_a_data[12:0], and silently dropped the other A-channel inputs. The vector is now 121 bits wide and covers every input that rule (f) names: i_a_valid, opcode, param, size, source, address, mask, all of a_data, instr, intg_flip, d_ready, i_gpio and i_strap_en. This strengthens the check. rst_ni is left out on purpose: its assertion is asynchronous by specification (INT-RST-001), and the old checker never covered it either.

With GpioAsyncOn=0 the test bench drove every input right after the falling edge of clk_i. Contract CHK-011 rule (f) and INT-CLK-002 require these inputs to change only just after rising edges. With GpioAsyncOn=0, the TL-UL A-channel driver (_a_loop), the i_d_ready driver (_d_loop), i_gpio (set_gpio and gpio_pulse) and i_strap_en (Env.reset, strap_sequence and the regression strap phase) now drive 1 step after a rising edge, through the new helper Env.drive_sync. Sampling is unchanged: ReadOnly at the falling edge. Edge numbering stays the same, because a value driven after rising edge N is first sampled at N+1, which equals edge() at the falling edge that follows. In set_gpio, gpio_pulse and the strap code, edge numbers are taken from the value returned after the drive. gpio_pulse still keeps v_on for exactly n edges. Runs with GpioAsyncOn=1 are unchanged: drive_sync drives at once there, and the loops keep the falling-edge drive. No expected value or check was changed.

notes:
I changed four files and fixed all three faults. Nothing was simulated, so none of these changes has been run yet. No assertion, cover point, test, expected value or CHK reference was removed or relaxed, and no assumption was added.

Fault 1 (CHK-006, nnc_chk_intr.sv): while an INTR_ENABLE write is outstanding, the checker now skips only the bits that write turns from 0 to 1, from its A handshake to its D handshake. The existing masks at Ed and Ed+1 are unchanged. Two things to know:
- A write that ends with d_error=1 is also masked while it is outstanding, because the error is only known at Ed. From the next edge those bits are checked again.
- The checker tracks only one pending request (an existing limitation). If the design accepts a second request before the first INTR_ENABLE write completes, the first write's bits stop being masked before its Ed.

Fault 2 (CHK-008, nnc_chk_reset.sv): the check now starts at the first reset assertion (first falling edge of rst_ni, or first clock edge with rst_ni=0) and stays on from then. So only the t=0 edge, before any reset, is skipped. The hit counter now counts the edges where the check is active, and the fail message prints the six output values. I chose this checker-side fix over the preferred test-bench fix for two reasons:
- The clock's first rising edge is at t=0, and start_clock/reset_dut live in nnc_cocotb.py, which I may not change. So rst_ni cannot be asserted before that first edge.
- Driving rst_ni=1 from time 0 would run the design unreset for some cycles, while the rst_ni=1 checks (for example CHK-001) are active.

Fault 3 (CHK-011 rule (f)):
- **Test bench:** with GpioAsyncOn=0, all inputs now change 1 step after a rising edge, through a new helper Env.drive_sync. This covers the A channel, i_d_ready, i_gpio and i_strap_en. Sampling and edge numbering are unchanged, and runs with GpioAsyncOn=1 behave exactly as before.
- **Checker:** the rule (f) vector in nnc_chk_tlhost.sv is now 121 bits and covers every input except rst_ni. rst_ni is left out because its assertion is asynchronous by spec (INT-RST-001), and reset_dut releases it at a falling edge. The old 49-bit vector did not cover it either.

Edits outside verif/ that I was not allowed to make:
- contract.json:413, the CHK-006 behaviour text: it should say that bits an outstanding INTR_ENABLE write sets from 0 to 1 are not checked between its A handshake and Ed+2.
- contract.json:441, CHK-008 (optional): it should say the check applies from the first assertion of rst_ni.
- Spec D-018/D-004 (optional): state that a register write may take effect at any time between its A handshake and its response.
- Spec D-016 (optional): state that the reset checks apply from the first assertion of rst_ni.
